messages:
maria_sales: Hey team — ACME (POC) just flagged a blocker. Their security team refuses to allowlist our pool IPs. They prefer mutual TLS (client certs) or a cert-based auth model instead of static IP allowlisting. Can Dedicated endpoints support client cert auth, or what are the practical workarounds for the POC?

devon_se: Quick summary: Hosted API — no mTLS. Dedicated endpoints — typical options are (1) provide static egress IPs from the Dedicated pool (preferred), (2) recommend Private/VPC so the traffic terminates in their network, or (3) customer fronting proxy that terminates client certs and talks to us from a stable IP. We don't have an out-of-the-box client-cert handshake on hosted endpoints today.

acme-netops: We can't stand up a reverse proxy for the POC due to procurement. They want to avoid changing firewall rules frequently. Is there any way Redwood can accept a client cert pinned to the endpoint for a short-lived POC?

sam_infra: @maria_sales FYI — we can allocate static NAT IPs per Dedicated pool if they commit to a reserved pool for the POC. That gives them a small set of IPs to allowlist on their firewall. mTLS as a first-class feature is only available for Private/on-prem installs at the moment.

riley_security: Security view: mTLS is doable but requires PKI lifecycle (issuance, rotation, revocation) and audit logging. For a short POC we could accept a self-signed client cert pinned on our gateway, but we'd need the security questionnaire signed off and an internal exception ticket. Also need to document revocation steps.

devon_se: If they take the static-IP route, share this sample allowlist snippet they can hand to their firewall team:

```
# Allowlist entries for Dedicated POC (example)
198.51.100.23/32  # egress NAT IP 1
198.51.100.24/32  # egress NAT IP 2
# Allow outbound to: api.redwood.example.net (443)
```

devon_se: If they insist on client certs for the POC, here's a minimal curl example we can accept for testing (assuming we enable a temporary cert):

```
curl --cert client.pem --key client.key \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  https://dedicated-pool-123.api.redwood.example.net/v1/generate
```

alex_ae: ACME team also asked about rotation schedule. For POC we can do a 7-day cert and rotate once during test. They need instructions on how to produce a CSR.

sam_infra: Action items: (1) I'll open an infra ticket to reserve a small NAT block for the POC and confirm the exact IPs (eta 24h). (2) @riley_security can you start an exception request if we go the self-signed cert route? (3) @devon_se please draft the step-by-step for the customer (allowlist + cert flow) and include curl examples.

riley_security: I'll file the exception and attach the minimal risk assessment. If Infra can provide static IPs, that's the least friction.

devon_se: Drafted steps (I'll send in a follow-up thread):
- Customer confirms whether they can accept 2–3 static IPs.
- If yes: we provision Dedicated pool nat IPs, we send allowlist and test curl.
- If no and they want certs: Security exception + temporary self-signed cert process (CSR -> client cert) for POC only.

acme-netops: OK — we'll try to get firewall sign-off for static IPs first. If not, we'll request the CSR template. Please ping once IPs are available.

maria_sales: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll update ACME and schedule a short call tomorrow after Infra confirms the IPs. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: [deploy] dedicated-pool-123 requested by sam_infra — ticket #INF-4821 created

sam_infra: Ticket INF-4821 shows 2 IPs reserved: 198.51.100.23, 198.51.100.24 — confirming with netops now.

maria_sales: Closing loop — call scheduled 2025-10-02 15:00 PT. Devon, can you bring the CSR template if we need it?

devon_se: Yep, I'll have the CSR + short checklist ready.

riley_security: I'll also bring the exception doc so ACME has the checklist for the POC.

maria_sales: Thanks all.
